_comment: Which iOS simulator runtimes this automation platform supports.
This is a RANGE, not a pin. Any iOS runtime from min_ios to max_ios works;
nobody needs to download a specific version to run the platform. Whatever
runtime shipped with your Xcode is almost certainly fine.
Read by scripts/doctor.sh, which warns if a machine has no runtime in range.
Nothing enforces a version at RUN time on purpose: the platform resolves and
boots whichever simulator the machine actually has (see _resolve_ios_device
in automation/projects/builder.py), and test capabilities intentionally omit
platformVersion so Appium does not demand an exact match.
To support a newer iOS later, raise max_ios here and re-run doctor.sh.

notes.why_16: Floor of what the XCUITest driver and these scenarios are known to work on.
notes.why_26: Current newest public iOS. Raise when a newer one ships and is verified.
notes.device_family: Any iPhone or iPad simulator. iPhone is preferred automatically when several are available.
notes.not_a_dependency: iOS runtimes are multi-GB Apple downloads and cannot be installed by pip or npm. requirements.txt has no reach here; this file only declares what is acceptable.
